summary: Import-time Windows PE dropper in package advertised as a placeholder streak utility
details: index.mjs contains a large base64-encoded array (P1) whose decoded bytes are a Windows PE executable (MZ header, DOS stub string). On module import, the code base64-decodes the array into a Buffer and writes it to disk via writeFileSync. The package's declared purpose is a dependency-free streak/habit counter and the README states the implementation is a placeholder, yet the shipped 347 KB module consists almost entirely of the encoded PE payload with no functional streak/habit code. The behavior is consistent with an opaque-binary dropper: an executable payload with no relation to the stated purpose is dropped onto the installer's filesystem at import time, concealed via base64 encoding.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
